edges.label: Both criticize the unclear timetable
edges.reason: The FT editorial and Zelensky both object to a lack of a clear route and date. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: This matches their criticism, not every proposal each speaker supports.

edges.label: Shared conditional wording
edges.reason: Both describe an invitation depending on allies’ agreement and conditions being met. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: Sputnik describes a reported draft; FT discusses agreed wording. The source document versions and sources differ.

edges.label: No invitation now versus no date
edges.reason: A Lithuanian ambassador predicts no summit invitation; a reported draft gives no timetable.
edges.caveat: These compatible claims are not identical: absence of a date does not itself rule out an invitation that day.

edges.label: The multiyear program gives a concrete support commitment
edges.reason: TASS reports Stoltenberg announcing adoption of a multiyear assistance program. That is a specific policy commitment supporting the continued-assistance pledge reported by European Pravda.
edges.caveat: Stoltenberg is the source for both statements, made at different points in the summit day.
edges.direction_reason: T01 supplies the specified support for EP02.
edges.unsupported_parts: Completed deliveries or the length and content of every future aid package.

edges.label: Same support plan, different details
edges.reason: Both report Stoltenberg’s long-term support plan. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: One emphasizes adoption, the other the intended preparation of forces; the announcements come at different points during the day.

edges.label: Aid as deterrence versus aid as prolonging fighting
edges.reason: The FT recommends lasting assistance to protect Ukraine and deter new aggression. Experts quoted by Global Times characterize Western commitments as prolonging bloodshed. These are opposing evaluations of the purpose and effects of Western assistance.
edges.caveat: The FT discusses protection including after the conflict; the experts discuss the ongoing war. Assistance could prolong present fighting and deter future aggression. Review the time horizon before treating the forecasts as incompatible.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: FT03 is proposed to contradict GT03. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Same Wednesday council plan
edges.reason: Both report the NATO chief’s schedule for the council meeting. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: Same speaker and planned meeting, not two independent observations of an event already completed.

edges.label: Same new council proposal
edges.reason: Both describe the NATO-Ukraine Council as a body for closer political relations. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: Stoltenberg is the common original source; the intended role does not confer NATO membership.

edges.label: Same planned council appearance
edges.reason: Both say the first council meeting with Zelensky was scheduled for Wednesday. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: A schedule is not proof that the subsequent meeting occurred.

edges.label: NATO drawn closer versus rising divisions
edges.reason: CNN describes NATO as closer than at any time since the Cold War. Global Times highlights rising divergences behind an outward show of solidarity and the prospect of serious disunity. The passages offer contrasting assessments of alliance cohesion at the summit.
edges.caveat: Comparatively stronger overall cooperation can coexist with disagreements on particular policies and future risks. Review the baseline, policy areas and distinction between current conditions and forecasts.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: CNN04 is proposed to contradict GT01. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Reported French opposition supports the approval obstacle
edges.reason: CNN reports Macron’s opposition to the Tokyo office. That supplies a reason for the difficulty of unanimous approval described in Global Times.
edges.caveat: CNN cites NHK and Global Times cites Nikkei. Independent source access is not established.
edges.direction_reason: CNN03 supplies the specified support for GT05.
edges.unsupported_parts: The eventual NATO decision or every reason for France’s position.

edges.label: An office presented as arranged versus a delayed decision
edges.reason: China Daily’s guest writer says NATO has already persuaded Japan to open a Tokyo office the following year. Global Times reports that NATO would defer its decision until autumn or later. The comparison flags an apparent arranged-versus-pending contrast in the office plan.
edges.caveat: Japan’s willingness to host and NATO’s unanimous institutional approval are separate decisions. The two accounts can both be accurate if they refer to different approval stages. Review the decision stage meant in each passage.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: CD02 is proposed to contradict GT04. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Opposing evaluations of Nordic NATO expansion
edges.reason: The FT editorial welcomes Sweden’s membership progress. The China Daily guest author evaluates Nordic NATO enlargement as harmful to regional stability.
edges.caveat: This proposed comparison concerns opposing evaluations. Stronger NATO defenses and more confrontation could occur together, so the factual forecasts need separate review. The guest author’s views remain attributed.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: FT04 is proposed to contradict CD01. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Turkey’s reported decision supports the progress account
edges.reason: Global Times reports Turkey agreeing to clear the way for Sweden’s membership. That supplies a concrete step supporting the FT’s account of progress in breaking the impasse.
edges.caveat: The arrow supplies an event detail relevant to the editorial’s account.
edges.direction_reason: GT02 supplies the specified support for FT04.
edges.unsupported_parts: The FT’s positive evaluation or the predicted effects on NATO defenses.

edges.label: Named disagreements support the account of divisions
edges.reason: The FT identifies specific disagreements over Ukraine’s membership among the US, Germany and other allies. Those examples support the present-divisions component of the Global Times account.
edges.support_scope: Existing policy disagreements within NATO in GT01.
edges.caveat: The FT discusses the membership wording. Global Times also discusses other sources of tension.
edges.direction_reason: FT05 supplies the specified support for GT01.
edges.unsupported_parts: Future serious splits or an inability to resolve the conflict.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a supporting claim to the claim receiving support. Grey comparisons have no assigned direction. Solid red arrows point from a source claim to a target claim it is proposed to contradict. Red direction follows the analyst-assigned comparison order. Every proposed conflict retains its reasoning and scope limits for human review.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs.
